alex_m: heads-up — while onboarding `hf/my-open-model` into Redwood embedding pipeline, reranker metrics tanked. quick local bisect shows an off-by-one shift in pooled vectors vs HF baseline. looks like pooling index mismatch after tokenizer conversion.
rachel_k: ugh. can you paste a tiny repro? is it from special tokens (bos/cls) or truncation policy? @michael might have seen this with the chat templates last week.
alex_m: minimal repro below. converting tokenizer with our converter script then comparing token ids and pooled index. noticed `cls` moved one slot because converter inserts pad before cls in some cases.
```bash
# convert
python tools/convert_hf_tokenizer.py --hf hf/my-open-model --out /tmp/rw-tok
# inspect
python - <<EOF
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('/tmp/rw-tok')
s = 'Hello world'
enc = t(s, return_tensors='pt', truncation=True, padding=True)
print('tokens:', t.convert_ids_to_tokens(enc['input_ids'][0]))
print('ids:', enc['input_ids'][0].tolist())
# pooled index we use for CLS pooling: expected 0 but got 1
EOF
```
sample output we saw:
````
tokens: ['<pad>', '<s>', 'Hello', 'world', '</s>']
ids: [1, 0, 345, 678, 2]
````
expected HF tokenization: `['<s>', 'Hello', 'world', '</s>', '<pad>']` so CLS at index 0 in HF but index 1 after conversion.
this breaks our embedding-pooler when configured to `pooler=cls` (we pick index 0).
michael: that matches what I remember — our HF->Redwood bridge sometimes normalizes pad placement to 'left' padding for older tokenizers. check `tokenizer.padding_side` and `tokenizer.truncation_side` and also `add_special_tokens` logic. also some HF chat templates set `bos_token` != `cls_token` and the converter didn't map them, so cls ended up as a separate token later in sequence.
samantha: quick patch idea: in convert_hf_tokenizer.py, when special_tokens_map has both bos_token and cls_token, explicitly set `tokenizer.cls_token = tokenizer.bos_token` if model uses same semantics; otherwise keep mapping but preserve padding_side. patch snippet I used locally: 
```py
# force left->right consistent padding and preserve cls pos
if hasattr(tokenizer, 'padding_side') and tokenizer.padding_side == 'left':
    tokenizer.padding_side = 'right'  # match HF default ordering for our pooler tests
# ensure cls maps to bos when chat template expects that
if tokenizer.special_tokens_map.get('bos_token') and not tokenizer.special_tokens_map.get('cls_token'):
    tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'cls_token': tokenizer.special_tokens_map['bos_token']})
```
worked for me in smoke tests.
alex_m: thanks — after applying that patch and re-running the small eval, reranker MRR on the validation set jumped from 0.62 -> 0.75 and mean cosine offset went from 0.02 -> 0.003. added a quick unit test to assert pooled index for a few canonical prompts.
rachel_k: great. can you add a test that covers chat templates (user/system/assistant) too? those are the trickiest — sometimes the converter maps `<|system|>` to different tokens. also add explicit mapping checks in the config.json we produce: include fields `cls_token`, `bos_token`, `padding_side` so runtime doesn't have to guess.
michael: also FYI our quantization runs exposed timing differences but not tokenization. quantization experiment notes: quantized runtime removes some pre-tokenization normalization in the pipeline for speed — that might mask an existing mismatch, so good to make tokenizer canonical before quant. add to checklist: canonicalize tokenizer -> run unit tests -> then quantize.
samantha: pushed a small PR with the conversion patch and tests: https://git.redwood/infra/convert-tokenizer/pull/42 (WIP). deploy-bot: deploy pipeline kicked off for infra/convert-tokenizer PR 42 (ci: unit, smoke).
deploy-bot: build 2026-03-20T15:01:12Z succeeded (lint, unit, smoke).
alex_m: confirmed PR fixes staging model. next steps: (1) merge PR, (2) add a migration note to model-onboarding guide about special_token mapping and pooling assumption, (3) add a non-regression embedding metric to onboarding pipeline (delta MRR threshold). I'll open a follow-up ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
